name: An Introduction to Philosophy of Science
description: This course introduces students to foundational questions about science as humanity’s most influential knowledge-producing enterprise. A central theme is the epistemic authority of science: what justifies its privileged status as a source of reliable knowledge? Topics include the demarcation between science and non-science, the methodological principles of scientific reasoning, and debates concerning objectivity, disagreement, theory change, and scientific progress. The course also examines the status of core concepts such as explanation, laws of nature, causality, and natural kinds, as well as discussions on scientific realism, the role of observation and experiment, the use of models, and the influence of values and social context on scientific inquiry.
